page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a memory-allocated virtual machine belonging to the N1 server family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64 with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is configured with 26.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 6.5 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place this server in the lower tiers of modern compute capacity. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, consistently rank in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show read-only speeds of 162.39 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.86 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, while write speeds reach 21.97 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks, including gzip and bzip3, also register in the lower percentiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on legacy Intel Xeon hardware, making it a qualitative option for workloads requiring more RAM than raw compute power without the premium of newer generation architectures. It is best suited for moderate database operations, caching layers like Redis, basic web serving, and memory-bound utility tasks that do not demand high-frequency CPU performance or advanced vector instructions.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a memory-allocated virtual machine from the legacy N1 family, featuring 4 vCPUs and 26.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.3 GHz with 2 physical cores and hyper-threading, it provides a dedicated CPU allocation with a 45 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its compute and memory performance in the lower percentiles, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores falling in the bottom 25%. Consequently, this server is qualitatively positioned as a cost-effective option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance compute. It is best suited for moderate database hosting, caching layers, and general-purpose memory-bound applications.
